title: Recovery of a closed subspace of relative Proj by a homogeneous ideal
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $X$ be an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], and use the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $\mathcal A=\bigoplus_{n\geq0}\mathcal A_n$ be a commutative unital graded $\mathcal O_X$-algebra [def-trf-etale-graded-module-algebra] whose components are quasi-coherent [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. Assume the structure morphism $p:P_X(\mathcal A)\to X$ of [lem-sfb-space-relative-proj-scheme-tests] is quasi-compact, meaning its pullback over every affine scheme has quasi-compact source. For every closed subspace $i:Z\hookrightarrow P_X(\mathcal A)$, where closed means representable by closed immersions on scheme tests [def-weil-closed-immersion], there is a homogeneous ideal $\mathcal I=\bigoplus_{n\geq0}\mathcal I_n\subseteq\mathcal A$ with each $\mathcal I_n\subseteq\mathcal A_n$ quasi-coherent and with products $\mathcal A_m\mathcal I_n\subseteq\mathcal I_{m+n}$, such that the quotient-induced closed immersion identifies $$P_X(\mathcal A/\mathcal I)=Z$$ as closed subspaces of $P_X(\mathcal A)$. Quotients and their induced closed immersions are [lem-sfb-space-qcoh-affine-chart-calculus, lem-sfb-space-relative-proj-quotient-closed-immersion]. No quasi-compactness or quasi-separatedness of $X$, finite presentation of $i$, or finite generation of the graded algebra is assumed.

source.place: Tag 085L, lemma-closed-subscheme-proj; existential consequence of the canonical graded kernel construction in the statement. The quotient-induced identification is the statement of the lemma.

proof.text: First $p$ is separated. On an affine etale chart $U\to X$, its pullback is $\operatorname{Proj}C\to U$ by [lem-sfb-space-relative-proj-scheme-tests] and [def-nagata-relative-proj], with $C=\bigoplus_n\mathcal A_n(U)$. The scheme $\operatorname{Proj}C$ is separated over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ by [lem-trf-proj-separated]. Its diagonal over $U$ is the pullback of its absolute diagonal along $\operatorname{Proj}C\times_U\operatorname{Proj}C\to\operatorname{Proj}C\times_{\mathbf Z}\operatorname{Proj}C$, hence is closed by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change]. The atlas may be refined by affine opens. Apply [lem-trf-space-qc-separated-etale-local] to this family: the pulled-back sources are quasi-compact by the hypothesis on $p$, and their maps are separated as just proved. Thus $p$ is quasi-compact separated, without any compactness assumption on $X$.

source.place: Tag 084E (lemma-relative-proj-separated), used in Tag 085L, first paragraph.

proof.text: Write $B=i_*\mathcal O_Z$. By [lem-sfb-space-ideal-closed-subspace-correspondence], $\mathcal O_P\twoheadrightarrow B$ has a quasi-coherent ideal kernel $K$. Hence $B=\mathcal O_P/K$, the cokernel of $K\to\mathcal O_P$, is quasi-coherent by [lem-sfb-space-qcoh-kernels-colimits], with chart sections computed by [lem-sfb-space-qcoh-affine-chart-calculus]. Take $E_n,\psi$ from [lem-sfb-space-relative-proj-graded-twists] and put $F_n=E_n\otimes B$ for $n\geq0$. Each $F_n$ is quasi-coherent by the tensor clause of the chart calculus. Its products are $(x\otimes b)(y\otimes c)=xy\otimes bc$; the unit is the image of $1$. Composing $\psi_n$ with $E_n\to F_n$ and taking its adjunct gives $\alpha_n:\mathcal A_n\to p_*F_n$ [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors]. Products of compatible sections give the graded multiplication on $(p_*F_n)_n$, and $\alpha_{m+n}(ab)=\alpha_m(a)\alpha_n(b)$ because $\psi$ and $\mathcal O_P\to B$ respect multiplication. The direct images $p_*F_n$ are quasi-coherent by [lem-trf-space-qc-separated-quasi-coherent-pushforward] and step 1. Define $\mathcal I_n=\ker\alpha_n$. Its quasi-coherence is the kernel clause of [lem-sfb-space-qcoh-kernels-colimits], and the chart calculus computes it on affine charts; the displayed product equation gives $\mathcal A_m\mathcal I_n\subseteq\mathcal I_{m+n}$. Thus $\mathcal I=\bigoplus_n\mathcal I_n$ is the required kind of homogeneous ideal and $\mathcal A/\mathcal I$ is a graded quasi-coherent quotient, degree by degree. No assertion that sections commute with infinite coproducts is used.

source.place: Tag 085L (lemma-closed-subscheme-proj), canonical kernel and quasi-coherence paragraph; Tag 084D supplies the twisting algebra.

proof.text: Fix an affine etale chart $U\to X$, and set $P_U=P\times_XU$ and $Z_U=Z\times_PP_U$. The first is a scheme by [lem-sfb-space-relative-proj-scheme-tests], and the second is a closed subscheme by the meaning of a representable closed immersion. Restricting the direct-image chart diagram of [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors] to an etale object $V\to U$ gives exactly the diagram of charts over $P\times_XV$. Therefore $(p_*F_n)|_U=(p_U)_*(F_n|_{P_U})$ with the same evaluation maps. Restriction also identifies $B|_{P_U}$ with $(i_U)_*\mathcal O_{Z_U}$ by this diagram. The twisting comparison of step 2 and [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence] identify these objects, products and maps with the ordinary scheme objects. Since kernels are computed on affine etale charts [lem-sfb-space-qcoh-affine-chart-calculus], the graded ideal $I=\bigoplus_n\mathcal I_n(U)$ is precisely the kernel of $C\to\bigoplus_{n\geq0}\Gamma(P_U,\mathcal O_{P_U}(n)\otimes(i_U)_*\mathcal O_{Z_U})$, where $C=\bigoplus_n\mathcal A_n(U)$. This is restriction to an etale slice, not a claim of arbitrary nonflat base change for kernels or direct images.

source.place: Tag 085L, last paragraph: etale localization; direct-image restriction spelled out.

proof.text: Work on this affine base, writing $Q=\operatorname{Proj}C$ and $H=(i_U)_*\mathcal O_{Z_U}$. If $Q$ is empty there is nothing to compare. Otherwise its standard positive-degree homogeneous opens cover it by [def-pc-proj]: a relevant homogeneous prime misses a homogeneous positive-degree element. Since $Q$ is quasi-compact, select finitely many $D_+(f_j)$ covering $Q$. Replace $f_j$ by a positive power so all have the same degree $D>0$; the opens are unchanged because a prime contains a power exactly when it contains its base. By [lem-trf-proj-common-degree-twist-invertible], all $\mathcal O_Q(kD)$ are invertible and multiply as tensor powers. On $D_+(f_j)$ their generator is $f_j^k$: by the fraction normalization of step 2, multiplication by $f_j^k$ identifies $(C_{f_j})_0$ with $(C_{f_j})_{kD}$, with inverse division by that power. Put $T_j=C_{(f_j)}$ and let $J_j=\ker(T_j\to H(D_+(f_j)))$. The ideal/closed-subspace correspondence of step 2 identifies these with the actual scheme-theoretic ideals of $Z_U$ on the charts.

source.place: Reduction in divisors.tex Tag 0801 (lemma-closed-subscheme-proj), finite homogeneous cover and common multiple of degrees.

proof.text: The quotient-induced closed immersion $Q'=\operatorname{Proj}(C/I)\hookrightarrow Q$ is the scheme test of [lem-sfb-space-relative-proj-quotient-closed-immersion]. On $D_+(f_j)$ it has ideal $J'_j=\{g/f_j^e:g\in I_{eD},\ e\geq0\}\subseteq T_j$. Indeed its chart map is the ordinary map $C_{(f_j)}\to(C/I)_{(\bar f_j)}$ induced by the quotient. It is onto by lifting homogeneous numerators. A degree-zero fraction maps to zero exactly when $f_j^l g\in I$ for some $l\geq0$, and then it equals $(f_j^l g)/f_j^{e+l}$; this proves the asserted kernel formula directly from the localization relation [def-nagata-homogeneous-localization-degree-zero]. For $g\in I_{eD}$, its canonical section maps to zero in $\Gamma(Q,\mathcal O_Q(eD)\otimes H)$ by step 3. Trivializing by $f_j^e$ shows that $g/f_j^e$ vanishes on $Z_U\cap D_+(f_j)$. Hence $J'_j\subseteq J_j$. This argument retains the full ideal, including nilpotents.

source.place: divisors.tex Tag 0801, inclusion of chart ideals; quotient chart kernel written out.

proof.text: Conversely fix $f=f_0$ and a fraction $g/f^e\in J_0$, with $g\in C_{eD}$. On each $D_+(f_j)$ set $a_j=f/f_j\in T_j$ and let $t_j$ be the image of $g/f_j^e$ in the quasi-coherent module $H$ there. On $D(a_j)=D_+(f)\cap D_+(f_j)$, this image equals $a_j^e$ times the restriction of $g/f^e$, so is zero. Apply [pqf-lem-qcoh-compact-section-power-torsion] to the affine scheme $D_+(f_j)$, its quasi-coherent module $H$, regular function $a_j$ and section $t_j$. Its conclusion gives $N_j\geq0$ with $a_j^{N_j}t_j=0$. There are finitely many charts, so take $N\geq N_j$ for all $j$. The section $f^Ng$ of $\mathcal O_Q((e+N)D)\otimes H$ has coefficient $a_j^N t_j=0$ in the frame $f_j^{e+N}$ on every chart. The sheaf axiom makes it zero globally; hence $f^Ng\in I_{(e+N)D}$ by step 3. Thus $g/f^e=(f^Ng)/f^{e+N}\in J'_0$. The argument works for any chosen chart, so $J_j=J'_j$ for all $j$.

source.place: divisors.tex Tag 0801, reverse inclusion: uniform powers on a finite cover, with degree-consistent denominators.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-space-relative-proj-quotient-closed-immersion], $P'=P_X(\mathcal A/\mathcal I)$ is a closed subspace of $P$, and its base change to $U$ is exactly $Q'\hookrightarrow Q$. Steps 4--6 give equality of the ideal sheaves of $Z_U$ and $Q'$ on a standard open cover; they are therefore equal as closed subschemes. Apply this over an affine refinement of an etale scheme atlas of $X$. Its pullback covers $P$ by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. The correspondence [lem-sfb-space-ideal-closed-subspace-correspondence] identifies ideals of these closed subspaces on that cover with restrictions of their ideals on $P$. The two subsheaves of $\mathcal O_P$ are equal: a section lies in one if and only if it does after this cover, where both membership conditions agree. Thus their ideals are equal globally and the same correspondence gives $Z=P'$ as closed subspaces. If any test $Q$ is empty both closed subspaces there are empty. If $Z$ is empty, $B=0$ and $\mathcal I=\mathcal A$; if $Z=P$, the construction can have a nonzero irrelevant-torsion kernel, but the chart argument still gives the identity closed subspace. No reducedness or finite-presentation assumption occurred.

source.place: Tag 085L, final equality of closed subspaces after etale localization.

lean.statement: theorem space_proj_homogeneousIdeal_recovery {S : Scheme.{u}} (C : SpaceProjCoefficients S) (R : SpaceProjSystem C) (Q : SpaceProjQuotientSystem C R) {X : AlgebraicSpace S} (A : SpaceProjInput X) (hqc : ∀ (W : Over S) (g : schemeSpace W ⟶ X), IsAffine W.left → CompactSpace (spaceProjScheme W (C.scheme A W g).affine).left) (Z : AlgebraicSpace S) (i : Z ⟶ (R.realization A).space) (hi : IsRepresentableWith (fun _ _ p ↦ IsClosedImmersion p.left) i.hom.hom) : ∃ (B : SpaceProjInput X) (φ : EtaleGradedModuleAlgebra.Hom A.algebra B.algebra) (hφ : ∀ n : ℕ, Epi (φ.degree n)), (∀ n : ℕ, (kernel (φ.degree n)).IsQuasicoherent) ∧ (∀ (m n : ℕ) (V : X.EtaleSite) (a : (A.piece m).val.obj (op V)) (t : (kernel (φ.degree n)).val.obj (op V)), ∃ c : (kernel (φ.degree (m + n))).val.obj (op V), (kernel.ι (φ.degree (m + n))).val.app (op V) c = A.algebra.mul m n V a ((kernel.ι (φ.degree n)).val.app (op V) t)) ∧ ∃ e : (R.realization B).space ≅ Z, e.hom ≫ i = Q.map φ hφ
